gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions (probe-verified against the real WASM)

gaps.missing: import edges mislabeled usage_contextual instead of import_based — the classifier's references branch checks isImport but TS import edges are the dedicated 'imports' kind, which falls through to the usage_contextual default (the JVM-family finding, kotlin K8 / scala G1 analog)
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (typescript/import-edges) + mutants typescript/reclassify-import-tier and typescript/drop-import-edges CAUGHT (2026-08-27). The dedicated 'imports' kind now classifies as import_based (classifier isImport branch extended), matching kotlin K8 / scala G1.

gaps.missing: type alias RHS references lost — type Fn = (a: Id) => Id, type Pair = [Id, Id], type Rec = { next?: Rec } emit the Fn/Pair/Rec symbols but NO references to the RHS types (Id, Rec self-ref)

gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (typescript/type-alias-refs) + mutant typescript/drop-type-alias-refs CAUGHT (2026-08-27). type_alias_declaration RHS now emits type_alias references to the referenced types (param, return, tuple elements, self-refs).

gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (typescript/field-uses) + mutant typescript/drop-expression-uses CAUGHT (2026-08-27). member_expression/subscript_expression reads AND writes now emit Uses on the accessed member (isFieldAccess), matching scala G8.

Function-body destructured locals shadow same-named properties — the scope-blind reference is suppressed (module-level destructured names remain symbols).

gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (typescript/dynamic-import) + mutants typescript/drop-import-edges and typescript/reclassify-import-tier CAUGHT (2026-08-27). Dynamic import('./lazy') now emits an imports edge (module:item), and the spurious calls -> import edge is suppressed.

decisions.question: Async arrows reported returnType 'void' (expression bodies have no return statements; the T3 sync-arrow fix wired block-body inference only). Fix by Promise-wrapping inferred inner, undefined, or leave?
decisions.decision: RULED - FIXED: async ALWAYS returns a Promise (TS semantics). Expression bodies infer via TypeInferenceEngine.inferFromInitializer (literals/binary/ternary/await-unwrap); unknown inner degrades honestly to Promise<void>. Block bodies keep extractReturnType and wrap. Explicit annotations stay authoritative and are NEVER re-wrapped. Bonus: sync expression arrows now infer too (f2: () => 1 is number — T3's documented precedent is now actually true; pre-fix BOTH expression forms reported void). Pinned by typescript/async-arrow-and-iface-overrides (f1-f5) + mutant typescript/async-promise-void.

Snippet is the raw source text req['body']. Pinned by the b1/b2/b3 taint assertions + mutant typescript/bracket-taint-drop.

decisions.question: interface Spring extends Readable with same-name member emitted ZERO overrides — the class pass requires metadata.isOverride + a Class-kind parent. Found via the svelte-repo typescript lane (Spring.subscribe -> Readable.subscribe MISSING).
decisions.decision: RULED - FIXED: structural-tier in-file BFS (depth-10, mirroring the oracle's truth walk) over Interface-kind symbols' metadata.extends. Overload abstention: a name declared twice in one interface never pairs (no textual-signature truth in the analyzer — the oracle's sigCompatible gate owns that distinction). External/unresolved bases emit nothing. ALSO FIXED en route: extends targets strip type-args to the clean head + leaf segment (extends Spring->Readable<T> was bracket-polluted — groovy S1 heritage class). Parity probe: analyzer and deriveTreeEdges emit IDENTICAL edges on the Spring/Readable shape, plain .ts and .d.ts both. Pinned + mutant typescript/iface-override-drop.

decisions.node_type: object-literal duplicate-key members (#746, M49 web-family dup-key ruling)
decisions.question: TS emitted BOTH same-key object-literal members (keep-both: 2 `save` symbols, phantom first body's calls edges intact) while JS at runtime executes the LAST declaration and the JS analyzer's J3 contract is last-wins — same shape, different graph by file extension. Found via the web-family dup-key convergence sweep (#746).
decisions.ruling: Option A — last-wins family-wide. collapseDuplicateObjectMembers walks `object` nodes only (class bodies = overload territory, untouched; get/set pairs coexist on kind-keyed slots per the B5 accessor-slot contract; a plain member kills same-name accessor halves — data replaces the descriptor). Dead members are spliced from symbols pre-map-build; dead spans tombstoned and phantom calls/uses filtered post-walk by source+line (filterPhantomDupKeyEdges). Pinned by fixtures/typescript/dupkey-last-wins; mutant typescript/dupkey-keep-both dies on it.
decisions.evidence: dupkey-verify.ts (2->1 symbol, line-of LAST), dupkey-ts-shapes.ts (get/set coexist, class overloads untouched, phantom call dropped), F3 ts 58/58, F4 437/437

decisions.question: typescript published `references` and `uses` edges that the differential allowlist dropped, so NEITHER label was ever compared for this lane. Two finished oracles — script/m14/oracles/typescript-references.ts (599 lines) and -uses.ts (247 lines) — existed in the tree wired to NOTHING: zero imports anywhere in the repo. The lane was green because it was blind, not because it was correct.
decisions.resolution: UNRESOLVED, and deliberately not decided by fiat. Wiring both oracles plus the two allowlist entries (the "full mirror" the M49.G7 groovy note requires) makes the lane RED on a 20-file vue-core draw: 145 MISSING + 8 UNEXPLAINED on `references`, 206 MISSING + 30 UNEXPLAINED on `uses`, 1/1 on `contains`. The 351 disagreeing rows are MEASURED to decompose into four families rather than being 351 defects: 108 are a LABEL SWAP (the same mention published under the other label — the analyzer publishes a type-position mention as `uses` at conf 0.9, real-typescript-analyzer.ts:4776, while the references oracle derives it as `references`), 61 are names the analyzer routes to the `imports` label (verified against the tree: `references ComponentOptionsBase -> SlotsType` is MISSING because SlotsType is imported), and the residue — 13 `references` and 47 `uses` rows, all lowercase identifiers — is the contract question proper: the analyzer deliberately SUPPRESSES an edge to a locally-bound name (the locals/shadowed/parameter test at :4742) while both oracles publish local reads. Which contract is correct is a decision about the ontology, not about the code: script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts fixes the list of ten types but defines no semantics for uses vs references, so there is no authority in the repo to appeal to and the oracle must not be bent to match the analyzer, because an oracle derived from the analyzer cannot disagree with it. Left OPEN with the measurement recorded.

decisions.node_type: object_literal method_definition (const util = { run() {...} }) at any depth
decisions.question: Are object-literal shorthand methods members with their own scope, or opaque syntax to skip?
decisions.decision: Members of the owning variable at ANY depth (JD18-class, JS parity): extractObjectLiteralMethod creates a Method symbol with ownerName = the nearest variable_declarator name (util, local); calls inside attribute to the method itself (run->helper, deep->inside). Pre-fix: no symbols at module level ('symbol pollution' comment — false; the resolver's findEnclosingClassName walked through the function boundary out to the enclosing CLASS, so nested-object calls misattributed to the enclosing method — run->inside instead of deep->inside). Function-body declarators whose value is an object literal descend (W1 exception to the locals rule); the declarator symbol stays suppressed.
decisions.evidence: probe ts-scope-probe/ts-w1-attr 2026-09-08; JS parity probe (method:deep + deep->inside); fixture typescript/object-literal-members; mutants reintroduce-module-leaf-attr + reintroduce-nested-misattr

decisions.question: What target does a computed member call emit?
decisions.decision: SKIPPED (JS family contract): the callee is not a clean name — the raw subscript text ('nodeTransforms[i]') is a target no symbol index can join. vue-core transform.ts had 2 such fabrications pre-fix; BaseTransition.spec.ts has 4 shapes. The oracle mirrors the skip (deriveTypeScriptEdges skips subscript callees — mismatch showed as 1 fake MISSING).
decisions.evidence: probe ts-subscript + ts-w2-live (2 artifacts in transform.ts); fixture forbid handlers[mode]; mutant reintroduce-subscript-call-targets

decisions.node_type: static_block body + property_definition initializer calls (static { warm(); }, count = Logger.init())
decisions.question: Which source do static-block / field-initializer calls attribute to?
decisions.decision: The CLASS (J5, JS parity): resolveRelationshipSymbol binds class_declaration to its symbol so static blocks and property initializers (which have no enclosing function) attribute to the class leaf (Service->warm, Service->init, instantiates Service->Handler). Pre-fix they fell through to the module leaf. Method bodies resolve to the method first, so this never misattributes method calls. Owner lookup returns the symbol (not a bare name) to satisfy the resolver's contract.
decisions.evidence: probe ts-static-init vs ts-j5probe (JS side: Service->init); fixture expectRelationships Service->init/warm + instantiates Handler; mutant reintroduce-module-leaf-statics

decisions.question: Does a pair-valued arrow get its own call-source scope?
decisions.decision: Module-leaf fallback on BOTH analyzers (JS probed identical: 'pair -> run') — family-consistent behavior, not a defect. The object's shorthand methods are the member contract (TSD7); pair-valued arrows are value functions of the property, their calls fall back to the module leaf until a consumer contract needs them. Not gated (ruling without fixture is allowed only for verified no-defect rulings; recorded here for the family ledger).

No fixture possible (outputs are bare names — same-name collisions are indistinguishable downstream either way), so this is a hygiene fix verified by inspection + typecheck + unchanged green suite, documented here instead of gated. decisions.question: M49 W4 rotated-sample finding (ledger T2): all 19 unexplained .d.ts edges in the svelte repo are interface-property redeclarations in a derived interface (HTMLAttributes.ontoggle over DOMAttributes.ontoggle, BaseElement.name over BaseNode.name, Analysis.runes/tracing, Reaction.fn). The analyzer's heritage rule is intentional (kotlin/scala/java carry the same contract); the F5 truth registered only method_signature, so the ORACLE was blind - and #759's earlier disposition ('oracle already models truth') was true only for methods.
decisions.decision: RULED - the oracle mirrors the analyzer (M37.21 lockstep): `property_signature` joins the override member set. Class FIELDS stay out: a probe proves the analyzer emits no class-field overrides, so truth must not outrun it. The analyzer is unchanged.
decisions.evidence: fixture typescript/dts-interface-property-overrides (count==2 + forbid pins); mutant typescript/property-override-drop CAUGHT; F3 typescript 60/60; corpus re-probe at the fixed tree: svelte-repo typescript lane 0 unexplained (was 19). Second finding of the same probe (T3) fixed in the same wave: the subscript-callee and dynamic-import branches returned before the child recursion, dropping every call nested in their arguments (console[method](message.text()) emitted nothing; runtime-browser/test.ts MISSING) - fixture typescript/subscript-callee-nested-calls + mutant typescript/subscript-callee-nested-call-drop CAUGHT

decisions.question: M49 W13 (web-family private-member audit): the field-access Uses rule looks the member's name up in the declared-symbol set before emitting, and that set stores private members under their CLEAN name (`count` for `#count` - the documented spec-table contract). The rule passed the node's RAW text (`#count`), so the membership test was always false and the analyzer skipped the read BY ITSELF: this.#count emitted nothing, while this.count emitted uses read->count and while the private METHOD call correctly emitted calls run->#step. TS was therefore blind to every private field read in a codebase. Probe-proven (public/private/method-arg/private-call matrix), not inferred. Not corpus-visible in the pinned corpora (element-plus 0, vue-element-admin 0, vue-core 1 - and that one is inside a comment in packages/compiler-core/src/babelUtils.ts), which is why no sampled differential lane ever surfaced it.
decisions.decision: RULED - the declared-symbol lookup normalizes the `#` prefix (private members are stored stripped) while the EMITTED TARGET keeps the `#` spelling: that is the spelling the calls edge already carries (calls run->#step) and the one the javascript twin emits (uses Store->#update_version), so the web family agrees on one private-member spelling. Pinned by fixture typescript/private-member-reads (uses read->#count and uses bump->#version LOST pre-fix) with mutant typescript/private-read-raw-lookup.

label_coverage._description: Which relationship labels this lane actually COMPARES. The M60 label-coverage sweep (script/m14/verify-label-coverage.ts) reads the differential allowlist, runs this analyzer over a corpus sample, and reports every label the analyzer EMITS that the allowlist DROPS: such a label is compared by nothing while the lane still prints a percentage, because the dropped rows enter neither the matched nor the unexplained bucket. Each entry below is a label this lane publishes and does not compare.

declared_gaps.label: imports
declared_gaps.reason: The analyzer emits `imports` (an import mention routed to the import label) and the allowlist omits the label, so every one is invisible. Measured at 126 edges per 15 files on vue-core and 23 per 6 files. There is no imports oracle, so admitting the label today would turn invisible edges into UNEXPLAINED ones rather than into a measurement — the #910 shape in reverse. Closes when an imports oracle exists; until then the edges are published and unmeasured, which is stated here rather than hidden.
declared_gaps.closes_when: an imports oracle exists; then admit the label and reconcile

declared_gaps.label: exports
declared_gaps.reason: Same class as `imports`: emitted by the analyzer (116 edges per 25 files on vue-core), dropped by the allowlist, and no exports oracle exists. Closes with one.
declared_gaps.closes_when: an exports oracle exists; then admit the label and reconcile
